questions.question: Summarise the drawing conventions of Term 1: the five line types, the rules for scale and dimensioning, and the first angle arrangement of views.
questions.expected_answer: Line types: dark continuous for visible outlines, feint continuous for construction and projection, dashed for hidden detail, wavy for breaks, chain for centre lines and cutting planes. Scale: a standard ratio such as 1:50 chosen as the largest that fits, written in the title block, with drawing size equal to real size divided by the scale number. Dimensions: real sizes in millimetres without units, each once, outside the outline, numbers above the line, overall sizes outermost. First angle: front view shows width and height; the top view goes directly below it; the left end view goes to the right of it, each view on the far side from the face it shows; feint projection lines and a 45 degree mitre line keep views aligned.

questions.question: Summarise the forces and material properties of Term 1, stating where reinforcing steel is placed in a bent beam and how steel is protected from rust.
questions.expected_answer: Static loads are constant, such as dead load; dynamic loads move, strike or repeat and are several times more severe through impact and fatigue. Even loads spread; uneven loads concentrate at points and cause turning effects. Tension pulls, compression pushes; steel is strong in tension, concrete in compression; long thin compression members buckle. Bending stretches the outside of the curve and squeezes the inside, so steel goes near the tension face, low in a supported slab and high at a cantilever root; deeper beams bend less. Torsion twists; tubes and triangulated bracing resist it. Density, hardness, stiffness, flexibility, brittleness and toughness describe materials. Rust is iron plus oxygen plus water, faster with salt; paint is a barrier that fails at scratches, galvanising protects even when scratched, stainless steel protects itself, and design caps tubes and drains bases.

questions.question: Summarise the design process as carried out in the PAT, including the costing rules and the tender presentation.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: measure the site at several points, ask the users, analyse existing entrances against fitness for purpose, materials, safety and cost, collect real prices. Design: a brief stating product, users, purpose and place without the solution; testable specifications with numbers; constraints and design considerations; two different ideas; an evaluation instrument applied by the group; the winner developed; a working drawing checked against every specification; a flow chart with decision checks. Make: convert to model scale, build in order with checks before gluing, safely and neatly, with check sheet and photographs. Evaluate with the same instrument. Communicate: a tender presentation in IDMEC order within time, every member speaking, with evidence and honest answers, and fair scoring of other bids. Costing: materials, labour and transport from drawing quantities and sourced prices, rounded up, with 10 percent waste and 10 percent contingency, checked for arithmetic, sense and proportion.
